request.prompt: Edit the supplied HAVENLINE PROTECTIVE STRUCTURES board. Preserve its six-panel layout, orange timber/blue/stone winter material language, substantial GUARDWALK→FORTIFIED LOOKOUT silhouette progression, main stair geometry and navy presentation. Fix the occupied deck access in ALL views. TOP ROW GUARDWALK: REMOVE the entire inaccessible upper cross-braced equipment pedestal and its top socket/slab. In its place provide one OPEN OBSERVATION DECK whose floor is exactly flush with the main guardwalk. It may be slightly wider, but there is no second upper floor. Put a low waist-high rail on the exterior edges. The side facing the guardwalk has one wide OPEN entry with NO rail, X-brace, door or tall step crossing it. All supporting cross braces sit BELOW the occupied floor, not through the entry. A person can walk straight from the stair landing along the walk and onto the observation deck without climbing. Top-row EXTERIOR sees the wall and low-railed observation deck beyond, INTERIOR clearly exposes the continuous walkway-to-deck opening, ACCESS is high enough to see the single uninterrupted floor route and open railing gap. BOTTOM ROW FORTIFIED LOOKOUT: retain the strong masonry tower and blue roof but make its occupied observation floor FLUSH with the wooden guardwalk. On the side facing the guardwalk REMOVE the obstructing railing span and any raised sill. Show a broad open rectangular entry framed by upright posts only, leading onto the covered deck. Lift the roof on taller posts as needed so standing headroom is obvious: a believable full-height doorway-shaped space, not a low crawl opening. The other deck edges retain their low protective rail; do not remove all protection. Keep the same wide gap, floor height, post arrangement and headroom in the true rear and high ACCESS views; exterior may naturally conceal the inside entry. Preserve the safe open stair-top landing and covered supply alcove beneath the later deck. No weapons, ammunition, combat or targets; this is solely the unarmed protective architecture study. Fully frame every structure. Keep title, row names, view labels and footer ARCHITECTURE STUDY.
